verdict.tagline: Brutal tactical warfare where survival demands patience and precision.
for_you_if: you enjoy high lethality tactical shooters
you tolerate rough edges for great combat
not_for_you_if: you need robust offline singleplayer modes
you expect seamless hit detection and voice chat
you cannot tolerate severe stuttering and optimization issues

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial frustration with technical performance and server availability shifts into strong approval as playtime increases.

citations.review_text: Terrible experience out of the all the fps milsims i've played, plus the game is mostly dead with maybe 2 active servers
GREAT GAME BUT NOBODY IN THE SERVERS ALL DEAD , i been looking for over 3 hours and not seen anybody in servers lol
The game is pretty dead, couldn't find any servers and the finding match takes too long been waiting for 20 minutes.
I'm sure in its time it was a great game But at this time there is barely 3 servers that are English and are actually operational

It's a great game, but holy ♥♥♥♥, there is like 5 active servers, and the game is stuttery as hell, atleast on a GTX 4060. I played the hell out of this game on the Epic Store. If you can get past these issues this is a great Vietnam Era game to play with a small but great community.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks proper offline mode and bot support.

citations.review_text:
no servers online but 2 that are full 24/7, cant make my own or play with bots, that this game needs bot support and offline mode, its kind of insane they still have not added that ever since 2017 :(

Tripwire has the tendency of making good gunplay (the best gunplay of all time might i say) wasted on multiplayer games with little to no proper bot support, same is for red orchestra 2, that game has bot support but is horrible, and setting up matches in it is very mediocre, hopefully they add proper bots soon

Controls are very heavy and sluggish. Fair it is not a modern game, and was trying for a more tactical thing but it doesn't do that good. This game leans into the 'Nam thing, that being you have all the classic characters looking out of Apocalypse Now, Deer Hunter, Platoon...etc which is always cool. Gameplay feels like a budget game, and It feels abhorrent to play compared to any number of Battlefield esque game you can get for free nowadays (Delta Force, World War 3) 

Had some stuttering issues that I needed to troubleshoot out, no reason this nearly 10 year old game can't run ultra on a modern gaming rig but there ya go. $2 wasted, 2 hours wasted, uninstalled.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players pushing past the start navigate external tutorials and bot-populated servers.

claims.claim: The game lacks an in-game tutorial for new players, providing only links to external YouTube playlists.

citations.review_text: This game has a lot of potential, but unfortunately, new player onboarding is just nonexistent. There doesn't appear to be an in-game tutorial, just links to a long YouTube playlist. Text chat is the usual edgy teenagers and voice chat might? be working, but one or two people use it sparsely per match. If you're already experienced with realistic milsim shooters you might have a good time, but I got a little too frustrated going 1-20 with nobody to ask for help for 2 hours. Probably refunding.

audio was inconsistent and sometimes non existant when trying to chat with other players in a multiplayer game and the only help i could find since u couldnt talk to people in game to find a solution was yt and it was complicated as hell i remember playin dawn of war on disc when i was a kid playing on my moms pc if the game didnt work it just didnt work modern gaming is ass

claims.claim: Servers are populated with bots that take up player roles and feature useless AI.

citations.review_text: game play is fun but sluggish movement - painfully slow reloads and gren priming makes the engagement slow and mass bots on servers with useless ai and a the usual geo cheaters with wall hacks makes this a fun but dated experience. You end up playign mostly on limited roles as any roles with weapons and interesting options get grabbed by bots so limited experience can be made on all roles. When you find a server which is admin monitored and a fuill team it is still fun but this is less likely as time goes by. Reviews seem very one sided shich suggests priming but for 15 quid it is fun.

If hell let loose and battlefield had a baby set in Vietnam this would be that baby.

The servers are alive enough, play during the day and you'll have a few full servers, play at night and you'll maybe find two full; it's on the smaller side of a playerbase.

It's as far as I know entirely online but has bots that fill servers; BUT if you play with a full lobby and do a campaign then there is no other large scale mil sim like this.
From strategy to just running through the rice-fields this game captures the Vietnam war perfectly; The limb damage system and reactive ground system in this game helps add immersion too.

Overall I'd recommend this game to anyone who has a interest in Vietnam and likes mil-sims, It is on sale often aswell.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Combatants embrace fast-paced lethal engagements despite limited training areas and technical stumbles.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the training area is limited to a basic targeting range rather than being fully developed.

citations.review_text:
I played this game a bunch a few years ago and it was really fun, despite the efforts of players playing snipers. It ran stable enough and the only issue I had was Australian ping. It was face paced by punishing for carelessness, straddling a line of high intensity and high risk with high lethality. I enjoyed it, especially in the urban maps where I didn't have to worry as much about being killed by a sniper I couldn't do anything against. I especially enjoyed playing the RPG, but I wished the training area was a bit more develop than just being a targeting range. Regardless, it was fun and, most importantly, playable.

I reinstalled it a few days ago and oh boy what has happened to it? A few years ago it ran fine enough on my PC, the same PC I still have, and now half the time it's half-frozen, either refusing to authenticate with servers (and taking ages to do so) or it just randomly starts lagging out the entire game, down to 1 frame for each 10 seconds in some cases. It doesn't stop in the main menu, either, and it continues after I close the game (though Steam still registers it as running and I have to exit game a second time in my steam library to actually get it to shut down). I don't know what's happening. I know it's not an issue with my computer because half the time it runs as well as it did years ago, but the other half it runs like I'm trying to play it on a computer from the early 90s. I haven't been able to play a match for a day straight now because it just start lagging out so bad.

RS2 is the absolute epitome of Vietnam shooters, as I don't think there is too many to even begin with. It strikes a perfect balance between arcade style elements with fast paced gameplay but without the bullet sponge that those type of games bring. The graphics are good enough for what this game has to offer, they are by all means not perfect but they still look stunning in the jungles of Vietnam.

The multiplayer campaign mode is by far one of the best game modes that Tripwire has brought to the Red Orchestra/Rising Storm series, with a persistent territory map where players need to coordinate to choose what factions to play as, territory to attack and special abilities to use. As the multiplayer campaign goes on, each team will unlock better weapons and commander abilities depending on what stage in the war it is ranging from early, mid and late war. The gunplay on this game is also very good considering its more arcade style aspects, recoil isn't hard to control but weapons feel punchy enough and feel like they actually deal damage. On a lot of FPS games shotguns are absolutely useless at range but on RS2 they are very usable and insanely deadly. The aiming deadzone feature is also one of the best, where instead of your player moving their whole body to aim it uses their arms instead and the player can stay in the same position, I believe this feature stems from ArmA but I could be wrong.

There are 6 factions to choose from, for North Vietnam there is the PAVN/NVA and the NLF (Vietcong). These two factions have similar weapons and commander abilities to choose from. The North Vietnamese have weapons like the Type 56 AK, older soviet weapons like the Mosin-Nagant, PPSH-41 and weapons from the Indochina wars. The South Vietnamese side has access to the US Army, US Marines, ARVN and the Australian Army. The south Vietnamese side has a wider array of weapons to choose from depending on which faction with weapons ranging from the M16A1, CAR-15, M14 and the L1A1 SLR.…

citations.review_text: nothing like getting blown up, spawned in, napalmed, spawned again, and being headshotted by a bush on endless repeat.

The game also has some rough edges and doesn't have the visual polish of newer shooters

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term veterans deal with hit detection flaws, broken voice features, and team balance challenges.

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues with voice chat functionality not working properly.

citations.review_text: 99% of devs quit just before fixing voip for real this time

It's a few years old, so there are some things you will expect - certain buggy mechanics, weird glitching, and certain technical issues. Despite that, there has been a loyal fanbase that has kept the game alive, and for good reason. We see with the failure of other Cold War-era FPS games that many, old or new, come back to this classic. I do think despite it's "rust" as can be seen by some, it can easily be polished and has potential to grow well past it's age of release. What I wish most was a fix to VOIP and using voice chat. It's spotty at best, and negligible at worst. The game would move much smoother and easily more coordinated if people could communicate outside of the text box that fades away messages after a few seconds.

You should definitely get it, but given its age and a player base at most of 300 people, definitely try around the time of a sale. But if you think the purpose and content of this game is up your alley, you definitely should give it a try. It might be confusing and a bit difficult to 'click' with the game, but you'll eventually see the hype behind it and why its player base keeps coming back to the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that hit detection can be inconsistent and unreliable during matches.

citations.review_text:
After playing this game for almost 10 years it is still the best Vietnam shooter available hands down. Since its release no other title has come close to representing the theme of the vietnam war in such an immersive way.

In general the game aged very well. but there is some jank here and there like your character potentially getting stuck on small obstacles on the ground when moving, and the hit detection not always doing its job, but the gun play is still one of the best with a very short TTK. just the way i like it.

Despite the playercount being relatively low, i had no real issues finding matches in EU and NA region. So if you are buying this with the intent to play it in those regions finding a match should not be an issue. Can't talk for the other regions.

If you are really looking for a good vietnam war experience, look no further, just get this. you are not going to regret it.

Pros: 
- Unreal Engine 4. High enough details that you can finally see long distances.
- Gunplay is good. Sounds are punctual and sound powerful. 
- No sprint limit. Hold shift and run for as long as you want. 

Cons (Reasons why I am not recommending this game):
- Lag. Developers never fixed the hit detection issue. Hit someone 5 times in the chest? It didn't register and now you are dead. You will be extremely frustrated and threaten to uninstall the game over dying from situations where you "could" clearly hold and defend, but the guy peeked first and your shots into his chest only wound him.
- Teamwork. Is non-existent. 


Overall this game is alive because there are enough players to fill servers. But this game is effectively abandoned. It could use some quality of life updates but those are never coming. You could buy this for the Black Orchestra mod, but the hit detection is still an issue.

Hark. This could develop into an abusive relationship. Sometimes it's fun. Most of the time it is not. You win by not playing. If you start, watch out for signs of coming back to this game even though you don't feel like playing. Chasing after a "good game" when at most it is only "passable matches".

claims.claim: Reviewers experience challenges trying to select preferred in-game classes due to competition and connection speeds.

citations.review_text:
Such a good game. I just wish more people played the army men mode. If you like squad, hell let loose, or any other team based tactical shooters. You'll feel right at home. Only downside is trying to get the class you want. It can be a struggle sometimes, and for sure favors those who have faster internet and are quick on the draw.

Maps are on the medium side. Not as big/open as squad or hell let loose, but larger than isonzo.

Really good game! 
Just expect in-game chat to get really political really fast and you'll be fine honestly, same as Red Orchestra 2 but a lot more arcade-y, like a LOT more arcade-like

It's actually kind of impressive the step down they took for this one, I haven't seen anything of '83 yet but I can only imagine they went further with this if nobody is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with me about the time playing it- Red Orchestra 2 has tanks, this has helicopters, bit of a tradeoff but it's not too bad and has plenty of mechanics to pair with it anyway so you're chill

It's all good, some achievements are locked behind the green army men DLC which I haven't even touched yet, the base game is just that good of a game? There's a little P2W aspect, hardly though, you can purchase camouflage as the Viet Cong which arguably makes you harder to spot, you can unlock this after a few dozen hours anyway though so it's not all bad. 

Just get on and get into using local chat, it's a pretty quiet game today but I've genuinely met one of my best friends by roleplaying on local chat while everyone else ignored or chastised what I was doing. I know what I'm doing, I'm making friends :D

But yeah no if you've got a soft heart this isn't it for you either, dying sucks and you really get to hear it. Maybe not Verdun levels of death, Verdun does dying justice, but it can be uncomfortable. Though fwiw if you're here and reading this you're beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and gonna buy anyway just for the death rattles, so good on you. 

tl:dr don't play anything else, just get this one from Tripwire. RO2/RS1 is also good but not as many people are on them either- The gameplay is also a lot more brutal in the previous entry. So maybe go there if that's your thing, the deaths are "better" there too.

RIP the British Tim, accidentally flamed four teammates in a row and got banned from the community server near instantly
I applaud your efforts over the local chat my friend, good show, good show indeed

Just get on and get into using local chat, it's a pretty quiet game today but I've genuinely met one of my best friends by roleplaying on local chat while everyone else ignored or chastised what I was doing. I know what I'm doing, I'm making friends :D

But yeah no if you've got a soft heart this isn't it for you either, dying sucks and you really get to hear it. Maybe not Verdun levels of death, Verdun does dying justice, but it can be uncomfortable. Though fwiw if you're here and reading this you're beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and gonna buy anyway just for the death rattles, so good on you. 

tl:dr don't play anything else, just get this one from Tripwire. RO2/RS1 is also good but not as many people are on them either- The gameplay is also a lot more brutal in the previous entry. So maybe go there if that's your thing, the deaths are "better" there too.

I applaud your efforts over the local chat my friend, good show, good show indeed
